To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein-coding regions in the genome evolve by sequence change and by gene gain and loss.
the evolution of human protein-coding sequences has resulted in the emergence of functional categories that are more divergent than others, with a dynamic pattern of divergence over time.

(i) human proteins are highly diverged from their homologues in other organisms; (ii) this divergence is highest for regulatory proteins; (iii) the rate of divergence varies with the functional category of the protein; and (iv) this rate of divergence varies over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the human proteome and its functional divergence.
the functional consequences of sequence divergence in the protein-coding genes of the human genome.
the evolution of the protein sequences that encode the functions that are essential to human life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional protein divergence in human genome is a dynamic picture of the selective force.
human evolution has been characterized by an increase in complexity, and a decrease in robustness, with the evolution of Homo.

protein-coding regions in the human genome evolve by sequence and gene gain and gene loss, altering the content of the organism, which in turn gives rise to the enormous variety of metazoa that we see today.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protein evolution in human can be characterized as a dynamic balance between robustness and evolability.
human evolution is characterized by functional plasticity and core robustness.
the human genome has a high degree of functional plasticity in its regulatory processes, but a low degree in its core processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human-specific proteins, which are a small fraction of the human proteome, are enriched in functions that are not highly conserved across metazoa.
the functional diversity of proteins is a key determinant of the diversity of life on earth.
functional protein divergence is a key factor in the evolution of human and that this divergence has been shaped by a combination of selection pressures acting over different evolutionary distances.
